rules.rule:
#### Base image and version pinning
For every `FROM`, `RUN` install, `ADD`, and downloaded artifact this diff adds or changes, name the exact version it resolves to and cite the line.
A floating tag (`latest`, a bare major, a rolling channel), an unpinned package install, or a fetch with no checksum is a finding: state what a rebuild tomorrow could silently change.
When the repository holds more than one container build file, read the others: a toolchain, base image, or pinned version that this diff moves out of step with a sibling file is a finding, and cite both paths.

#### Privilege and capabilities
Name the user this image runs as at the end of the file and cite the line that decides it.
A build that stays root, drops to root and never returns, adds `--privileged`, adds capabilities, or widens filesystem ownership is a finding unless the diff states why that privilege is required.
Ask the same of anything the container executes at start: an entrypoint or command that re-escalates defeats a `USER` line above it.

#### Secrets and build context
For every `COPY`, `ADD`, and build argument, name what enters the image and whether any of it is a credential, token, key, or private file.
A secret passed as `ARG` or `ENV`, or copied in and deleted in a later layer, remains readable in the image history: that is a finding, cite the line.
A broad `COPY . .` is a finding when the context carries files the image does not need; name them or name the ignore file that excludes them.

#### Correctness and reproducibility
Does each `RUN` fail the build when a step inside it fails, or does a pipe or chained command swallow the failure?
Are package caches, lockfiles, and layer ordering handled so the build is reproducible and the cache invalidates when inputs change?
Name what happens on the first build where a fetched dependency has moved.

#### Spelling
Check for spelling errors in yaml-keys within this file; ignore the content of yaml-values.

#### Image and version pinning
For every `image:` and every `build:` target this diff adds or changes, name the exact version it resolves to and cite the line.
A floating tag or a digest-less image is a finding: state what a redeploy tomorrow could silently change.

#### Privilege, exposure, and secrets
Name every added capability, `privileged: true`, host network or PID namespace, host path mount, and published port, and cite the line.
For each, state what it exposes and why the service needs it; an unexplained one is a finding.
A credential written as a literal value, or mounted from a path the repository does not document, is a finding.

#### Operational correctness
For each service the diff adds or changes, name its restart policy, healthcheck, and declared dependencies.
Ask what happens when a dependency is slow or absent on first start, and whether the stack converges or wedges.

#### Documentation accuracy
Does every claim about behavior, commands, flags, defaults, file paths, and triggers match the code and configuration at this head? Cite the contradicting file:line for any mismatch.
A claim about branch protection, required checks, merge gating, or anything else that lives outside the repository is verified against the live API, not against another document.

#### One owner
Does the text restate a fact that already has an authoritative owner elsewhere (code doc comment, another doc)? Prefer a pointer over a copy.
When the text names an owner, open that owner: confirm it actually carries the fact, and grep for surviving copies of the same fact elsewhere - other docs AND code comments - because a change that declares single ownership without retiring the other copies has not achieved it.

#### Completeness
Does the change leave a stale statement elsewhere in the docs (grep for the old wording)? Check the whole repository, not the diff window: a consolidation typically leaves its worst copy standing outside the files it edited.
Sweep every carrier the fact can live in, not only prose under docs/: section headings, source comments, the worked-example sources a document points the reader at, interface files such as .wit, and vendored copies of any file the reader is told to copy. A phrase search cannot find a copy that states the fact differently, so open every hit and read the paragraph around it.

#### Absolute claims
For every absolute or exhaustive sentence in a changed file - "there is no X", "every Y", "the only Z", "all N", "the entire", "verbatim", "never", "always", a numbered count, or a list presented as complete - name the code, configuration, or live API response that proves it and cite it file:line; when nothing proves it, the finding is to weaken the sentence until something does.
Prefer a sentence that states the property over one that lists the members: a list is only the cases someone remembered, and it is a finding when a member the list omits is constructible.
